title: Circuit Satisfiability Distinguisher
statement: Let binary encodings of Boolean circuits and three-CNF formulas be given, together with a polynomial-time map that sends each canonical circuit encoding to the encoding of its associated formula and sends malformed circuit encodings to malformed formula encodings. Let an encoded maximization problem for these formulas have every canonical formula encoding as a valid instance, optimum at most $1$, and optimum equal to $1$ exactly when the formula is satisfiable. Suppose a polynomial-time algorithm always returns a feasible solution on valid instances and returns value at least $1$ whenever the optimum is at least $1$, and a polynomial-time test outputs the one-bit string indicating whether that algorithm's value is at least $1$. Then there exists a polynomial-time map that outputs true on every promised yes-instance of circuit satisfiability and false on every promised no-instance.
hypotheses_covered: A binary encoding of Boolean circuits
A binary encoding of three-CNF formulas
A polynomial-time reduction with the stated canonical-encoding and malformed-input behavior
Every canonical formula encoding is a valid maximization instance
The optimum of each encoded formula is at most $1$
The optimum is $1$ exactly when the formula is satisfiable
The algorithm is a polynomial-time map and returns a feasible solution on every valid instance
The algorithm returns value at least $1$ whenever the optimum is at least $1$
The threshold test is a polynomial-time map
The threshold test's output is exactly the one-bit indicator of whether the algorithm's value is at least $1$
